back: X Granger-causes Y if the past of X improves the forecast of Y, beyond what the past of Y already gives.

front: What are the two regressions in a Granger test?
back: Restricted: Y on its own lags. Unrestricted: Y on its own lags and the lags of X. Compare them with an F-test.

front: Null hypothesis of the Granger F-test?
back: All coefficients on the lags of X are zero. X adds no predictive power for Y.

front: Can Granger causality prove cause and effect?
back: No. It shows predictive value and time order. A hidden variable or instant effect can mislead the test.

front: Which column does statsmodels test as the cause?
back: grangercausalitytests tests whether the second column Granger-causes the first. Run both directions.

front: Name two preconditions for a valid Granger test.
back: Stationary data (difference trends) and a sensible number of lags. Check several lags.
